page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose cloud instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Haswell x86_64 CPU, it features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with dedicated core allocation. The hardware profile includes 15.0 GB of RAM (3.75 GB per core), 16 MB of L3 cache, and 100 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Instruction support includes AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2, but lacks AVX-512 extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the legacy CPU architecture demonstrates limited raw compute throughput, scoring in the lower quartile for multi-core processing (3669.99 stress-ng score) and single-core tasks (959.69 stress-ng score). While uncached memory throughput remains weak, cached small-block memory read bandwidth reaches an average 347.69 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect moderate performance in memory-bound operations, achieving 5.93 million Redis SET operations per second and average scores in database operations and text processing.

The instance offers dedicated resource isolation without thread sharing, avoiding CPU credit limits or burst contention. However, its older processor generation creates a clear tradeoff between low entry costs and constrained compute performance per vCPU. The b2-15 is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, lightweight web application backends, basic database tasks, and Redis caching layers where memory allocation is prioritized over intensive CPU processing.
description: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose cloud server configured with 4 dedicated physical vCPUs on an Intel Haswell x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It features 15.0 GB of memory, 16 MB of L3 cache, and 100 GB of local SSD storage under the KVM hypervisor. Benchmark results reflect entry-tier compute capabilities, placing single-core and multi-core CPU metrics in the lower quartile, alongside weak uncached memory throughput. Conversely, cached memory bandwidth and key application metrics show balanced capacity, delivering 5.93 million Redis SET operations per second and steady database performance. The absence of hyperthreading provides predictable dedicated vCPU allocation, though instruction sets are limited to baseline AVX and AES without AVX-512. The instance delivers cost-effective resource density for light database hosting, Redis caching, microservices, and general web application infrastructure.
